mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 8%) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in unemployment above 9% for two consecutive months signals labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the effect disappears during periods of strong GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 15% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over two months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases risk aversion and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change < -0.5% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 2% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages by more than 3% in the same month signals a broad-based demand expansion, which increases earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA + 3% AND RSAFS > 12-month MA + 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months.
